text: Binary search trees are a fundamental data structure used to store data in a way that allows fast lookup, insertion, and deletion. A binary search tree, often abbreviated BST, is a binary tree in which every node has at most two children, referred to as the left child and the right child. The defining property of a binary search tree is that for every node, all values in the left subtree are smaller than the node's value, and all values in the right subtree are larger than the node's value. This ordering property is what allows efficient searching, because at each step the algorithm can discard half of the remaining tree. Searching in a binary search tree starts at the root node and compares the target value to the current node's value.

text: A hash table is a data structure that stores key-value pairs and allows near-constant-time lookup, insertion, and deletion. It works by passing each key through a hash function, which converts the key into an integer called a hash code. That hash code is reduced modulo the table size to produce an index, called a bucket, where the value is stored. A good hash function should distribute keys evenly across buckets so that no single bucket becomes overloaded. If two different keys hash to the same bucket, this is called a collision.
